scores.scale: 0 unusable; 5 mixed but functional with significant friction; 7 good with noticeable rough edges; 9 excellent with little observed friction; 10 exceptional across assessed scope. Subjective holistic scores based on observed interaction, not wins, result score or inferred enjoyment. Overall is a judgment, not an arithmetic average.

controls.reason: Two-contact MOVE + FIRE drag and scene turning worked in visible patrol combat in both runs. Large anchored controls and tap aim helped. Small scene targets needed correction; fine manual aim, physical thumb reach and continuous held-burst rearming remain uncertain.

gameplay.reason: Observed loop has understandable recovery, coil-disable and deck-hold stages, named enemy feedback and useful pressure cues. Extensive route/tap assistance and short paused bursts made traversal/combat less demanding in this review; offscreen threat handling was less clear. No enjoyment inferred for memories, menus or other unassessed content.

presentation.reason: Cohesive rain-soaked industrial scene, teal/amber information hierarchy, convincing weapon silhouette and polished title/results composition at390x844. Dark structures sometimes obscure targets; audio and hardware rendering/performance unassessed.

usability.reason: Visible contextual HOLD ROUTE/APPROACH/RECOVER labels, saved-memory feedback, upload progress and clear START FRESH made both mission cycles understandable. Route occasionally presented a wall rather than useful context; many tool buttons remain untested.

readability.reason: Health/ammo and primary objectives stayed legible, and terminal results fit portrait. Fine amber threat labels, distant coil labels and muted enemy silhouettes demanded close inspection against busy dark architecture.

holistic_assessment: Good, accessible assisted mobile mission flow with strong progress feedback and cohesive presentation. Manual two-thumb combat was sampled successfully, but the narrow viewport and small distant targets create precision/readability friction. Two wins do not certify sustained comfort or physical-device quality.
